result.title: The Effectiveness and Durability of Pretraining Data Filtering in Protein Language Models
result.summary: Pretraining filtering is one of the most common safeguards for open-weight language models. Here we study its effectiveness, durability and scalability using the ESM-2 family of protein language models. We find that filtering viral proteins from the pretraining data meaningfully degrades masked language modelling, mutation effect prediction and long-range contact prediction on viral proteins, while largely preserving performance on non-viral proteins. These effects are concentrated among proteins from human-infecting viruses, and grow as we scale models from 8M to 3B parameters. As models increase in size, we find that stringent filtering becomes more effective. However, fine-tuning on sequences from the removed viral families restores the lost performance. Although the cost to recover performance increases with model scale, even for the largest models it costs about 80 USD of H100 time. This work establishes pretraining filtering as moderately effective at selectively degrading performance on viral proteins, but not durable against fine-tuning with modest computational resources and access to relevant data.

AI.brief_summary: 以 ESM-2 蛋白语言模型为对象，研究预训练阶段过滤病毒蛋白的效果、规模依赖与耐久性：过滤会选择性降低病毒相关任务的性能、随模型增大更有效，但少量微调即可恢复。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「训练数据筛选—特定能力选择性退化—再训练恢复」的评估思路，可能为 LVR 中训练期监督如何影响内部表示的信息保留、贡献分配与遗忘耐久性提供类比线索，但与视觉多模态推理主线距离较远，需人工核查。
